examples.english: The desire for status can be considered, at its extreme, a modern, collective disease. examples.translation: Located at ground zero, the Sé Cathedral, as it was commonly called, housed hundreds of sculptures scattered around its exterior and interior, most of them in marble, as well as an organ with around twelve thousand pipes.

Perhaps reinforced by the possessive pronoun seu (see above) in the snowclone Dona X e seu Y, as in Dona Maria e seu José (“Mrs. Maria and Mr. José”, literally “... and her José”), wherein seu establishes the man as the woman's husband, having eventually been reanalyzed as the counterpart of Dona; compare Dona Flor e Seus Dois Maridos (“Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands”), the title of a Brazilian book and film.

examples.english: The desire for status can be considered, at its extreme, a modern, collective disease. This occurs when the lack or scarcity of material goods represents self-loathing and proof of inferiority. To combat this feeling, some people throw themselves into the market like true consumer kamikazes.
examples.ref: 2007, Márcia Tolotti, As Armadilhas do Consumo, Elsevier Brasil, →ISBN, page 51:
examples.text: O desejo por status pode ser considerado, no seu extremo, uma doença moderna e coletiva. Isso ocorre quando a falta ou a escassez de bens materiais representa um autodesprezo e uma prova de inferioridade. Para combater tal sensação, algumas pessoas se lançam no mercado como verdadeiros kamikazes do consumo.
examples.translation: The desire for status can be considered, at its extreme, a modern, collective disease. This occurs when the lack or scarcity of material goods represents self-loathing and proof of inferiority. To combat this feeling, some people throw themselves into the market like true consumer kamikazes.

examples.translation: The adage “Hope is the last thing that dies” should be taken literally, i.e. hope should only die with its owner; it should accompany them until their last breath.

examples.text: Localizado no marco zero, a Catedral da Sé, como era comumente chamada, abrigava centenas de esculturas espalhadas em seu exterior e interior, a maior parte em mármore, bem como um órgão com cerca de doze mil tubos.
examples.translation: Located at ground zero, the Sé Cathedral, as it was commonly called, housed hundreds of sculptures scattered around its exterior and interior, most of them in marble, as well as an organ with around twelve thousand pipes.

sense_provider_metadata.etymology_text:
From Old Galician-Portuguese pay < *pade, child-speech forms of padre, from Latin patrem, the accusative of pater (“father”), from Proto-Indo-European *ph₂tḗr (“father”). Doublet of padre.
Compare mãe (“mother”), which underwent a similar phonetic reduction from its root (Latin mater), and, in addition, was nasalized, perhaps because it was more frequently used than this word.
Cognate with Galician pai, Mirandese and Leonese pai and Aragonese pai.
